summary.headline: Choice International Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% YoY to Rs. 319 crore, with PAT of Rs. 61 crore (up 26% YoY).
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs. 319 crore, up 34% YoY and about 1.6% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs. 114 crore at a 35.75% margin and PAT of Rs. 61 crore (19% margin). Management described the quarter as a steady start, with broking at 59% of revenue, advisory at 28% and NBFC at 13%. Management said Rs. 900 crore from NH Investment & Securities into Choice Equity Broking is expected in Q2 FY27, with growth from it expected from Q3. Analysts pressed on the flat sequential run-rate over the last three quarters, and management's answers on timing and quantification were largely qualitative.

financial_highlights.change: Management said EBITDA declined sequentially (analyst remark, not disputed)
+26.37% YoY; analyst noted PAT declined QoQ

financial_highlights.value: Rs. 45 crore; loan book Rs. 836 crore
Over Rs. 6,766 crore; 30 mandates under execution; 1 IPO completed in quarter

segments.name: Broking and distribution
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs. 197 crore, PBT Rs. 48 crore; demat base 12.94 lakh (+13% YoY); stock broking AUM Rs. 62,226 crore (+30% YoY); about 70,000 Choice Business Associates.

segments.name: NBFC
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs. 45 crore; loan book Rs. 836 crore; focus on secured MSME, microlap and rooftop solar lending; GNPA 3.78%, NNPA 2.74%, NIM 11.10%.

segments.name: Advisory / consulting
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs. 91 crore; order book Rs. 777 crore; subsidiaries won government mandates aggregating about Rs. 191 crore; government advisory net margin about 20%.

segments.name: Insurance
segments.commentary: Premium collections Rs. 80 crore (+5% YoY); policy volume 67,828 (+73%).

segments.name: Asset management (Choice AMC)
segments.commentary: Still in setup phase; focus on passive schemes this year, active schemes targeted by FY27-end; BEP targeted in 2-3 years; SEBI approval to act as investment manager for Wealthwave Capital Trust (CAT II AIF).

guidance_outlook: Management expects the revenue mix to move to about 50% broking, 40% advisory and 10% NBFC over the next couple of years, from about 60/30/10-12 currently.
Solar financing AUM targeted at about Rs. 150 crore by FY27-end; ROI on solar being brought down to about 15% from 17-18%.
Management said the Rs. 900 crore NH investment will be received in Q2 FY27 and that growth from it should show from Q3 FY27.

Management expects a further 50% profit growth in FY28 on top of FY27 growth, from last year's PAT base of about Rs. 238 crore. The 50% CAGR was referenced by analysts; management did not restate it explicitly.
IPPB partnership: systems integration expected by end of the month; customer onboarding from 1 September 2026; no revenue or PAT guidance yet.
Branches: management reaffirmed a target of 800 branches over 3-4 years; analyst-cited March 2027 estimate of 300-350 branches was accepted by management.
Mutual fund distribution AUM growth expected at about 30-35% YoY; AMC business to reach breakeven in 2-3 years, with no AUM guidance yet.
Investment banking: about Rs. 6,600 crore of current mandates expected to complete over about 1.5 years, dependent on market timing.
capex_capacity: Rs. 900 crore strategic investment from NH Investment & Securities into Choice Equity Broking; management said internal accruals fund expansion, with proceeds mainly for the MTF book and settlement funding.
Choice AMC received SEBI approval to act as investment manager for Wealthwave Capital Trust, a CAT II AIF focused on pre-IPO investments.
Branch network: about 210-220 branches currently per analyst; management expects 300-350 by March 2027 as teams are onboarded.
Dedicated IPPB-linked wealth onboarding to start from 1 September 2026 once integration is completed.
demand_pricing: Stock broking AUM up 30% YoY; demat additions up 13% YoY; insurance policy volumes up 73% YoY with premium up only 5%.
Solar financing is a highly price-competitive market; ROI being lowered to about 15%.
Investment banking: one IPO completed in the quarter; pipeline over Rs. 6,766 crore; timing depends on market sentiment.
Government consulting mix expected to shift from heavy infrastructure advisory to governance, IT and project management consulting.

qa_highlights.question: What strategic value beyond capital does the NH Investment & Securities deal bring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capital is the smallest part; the aim is integration with NHIS institutional strengths in Southeast Asia, US and Europe. Near-term synergy is serving NHIS institutional clients with Indian market activity, and later joint investment banking deals.

qa_highlights.question: What return or ROCE is targeted on the incremental NH capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said internal accruals are sufficient for expansion; the capital will mainly fund the MTF book and settlement funding, with returns from interest income and higher brokerage. No ROCE target was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the NNPA improvement came from recoveries versus upgrades?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the improvement to collections by the in-house collections team, which handles accounts that slip out of the sales team's control; no split between recoveries and upgrades was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is incremental NBFC lending secured and how is credit quality protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all lending is secured by collateral, with an in-house credit engine, physical verification and central credit re-verification before sanction.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA and PAT decline sequentially, and what is the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some of the quarterly growth pattern reflects market seasonality; it did not quantify the sequential change or give a run-rate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the solar financing AUM, disbursement and yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the AUM figure and said it would be disclosed later. It said the weighted ROI was 17-18% and is being reduced to about 15%, with a Rs. 150 crore AUM target for FY27-end. Management also called solar secured, not collateral-free.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AMC monetisation roadmap and product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: This year's focus is passive schemes; active schemes are targeted by FY27-end, with a proper growth phase from FY28. BEP is targeted in 2-3 years, with no AUM guidance yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IPPB partnership's contribution and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Integration is expected to finish by end of the month, with onboarding from 1 September 2026. Management declined to quantify revenue or PAT impact until volumes are visible from September.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Rs. 900 crore NH investment be received, and when does growth show?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the money will come in Q2 FY27 and growth from it should show from Q3 FY27; Q2 will also see some growth, though no number was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the NBFC segment still running given its low returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NBFC has a gestation period, with ROE expected to improve within about a year as milestones are met, and capital is allocated mainly to broking because of its higher ROE.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 100-branch opening target on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said teams are finalised and branches will open once staff leave their current employers. It reaffirmed 800 branches over 3-4 years and accepted an estimate of 300-350 branches by March 2027.

risks_watch: Sequential flatness: analyst noted revenue of about Rs. 300 crore and PAT of about Rs. 60-70 crore across the last three quarters, and EBITDA/PAT declined QoQ in Q1 FY27.
Execution on the NH Investment & Securities Rs. 900 crore receipt in Q2 FY27 and on the growth it is expected to drive from Q3.
IPPB partnership onboarding from 1 September 2026, with no guidance on size yet.
Branch expansion: about 210-220 branches now; reaching 300-350 by March 2027 needs about 100 openings in six months.
NBFC return profile: low ROE, with management promising improvement within about a year.
Solar financing: highly competitive pricing, ROI being lowered to about 15%, and AUM disclosure still pending.
Investment banking revenue depends on IPO market windows; roughly Rs. 6,600 crore of mandates over about 1.5 years.
key_quotes: Our focus remained squarely on execution, strengthening each business vertical, improving our institutional and distribution franchisee, building our product capabilities, and branding the platform through which we serve the client.
Ayush Sharma: It's little early to give a guidance on the revenue number from this partnership. Once we start on-boarding customers, we will be able to probably give you some guidance.
We are on track with our growth target of 800 branches over the next three to four years' time. So, that we will certainly achieve.
Ayush Sharma: Firstly, solar is also not a collateral-free business. We do take solar equipment as a collateral while financing to the customer.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the headline numbers and the NH Investment & Securities deal, but turned cautious and vague when asked for quantification: the Rs. 900 crore impact on growth, the IPPB revenue and PAT contribution, the reasons for the sequential EBITDA and PAT decline, the solar AUM, and the branch timeline. Its answers on timing were qualitative and repeatedly deferred to later disclosures.

adds.what: Branch network expansion to 300-350 branches by March 2027 (from ~210-220 per analyst), toward 800-branch target over 3-4 years
Dedicated IPPB-linked wealth onboarding, customer onboarding from 1 Sept 2026

growth.why: Management guides ~50% PAT growth in FY28 on FY27 growth (from ~Rs 238 crore FY26 PAT base) and a 30-35% MF distribution AUM growth, with the Rs 900 crore NH investment due Q2 FY27 and growth from it from Q3; backing is partial, as the NH funding, branch ramp (300-350 by March 2027) and 1 Sept IPPB onboarding have some timing, while the PAT and IB figures lack specific quantification.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin was 35.75% on Rs. 114 crore EBITDA, and EBITDA and PAT both declined QoQ; management gave no margin lever or run-rate, and analysts noted revenue flat at about Rs. 300 crore for three quarters.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branches go from about 210-220 to a 300-350 target by March 2027 (about 100 openings in six months), and the Rs. 900 crore NH investment lands in Q2 FY27 with growth from Q3; management said teams are finalised but openings depend on staff leaving current employers.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Stock broking AUM is up 30% YoY to Rs. 62,226 crore, demat additions 13% YoY, MF distribution AUM guided at 30-35% YoY, and IPPB onboarding starts 1 Sept 2026, though the flat sequential run-rate tempers near-term volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure given and capex is not a model driver; growth is funded by internal accruals and the Rs. 900 crore NH investment for MTF and settlement funding, so a further capital raise is possible but not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided another 50% PAT growth in FY28 on FY27 growth from a Rs. 238 crore base, and the Rs. 900 crore NH investment could lift the MTF book from Q3, but no quantified revision has been given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: EBITDA and PAT declined QoQ, management gave no reasons beyond seasonality and no quantified run-rate, and the Rs. 900 crore impact, IPPB contribution and solar AUM are all unquantified, which leaves room for a guidance reset.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: IPPB-linked wealth onboarding starts 1 Sept 2026 (Q2 FY27), active AMC schemes are targeted by FY27-end, and the solar financing AUM target is Rs. 150 crore by FY27-end, though the AUM is not yet disclosed.

rows.label: Consulting order book Rs. 777 crore and govt mandates ~Rs. 191 crore
rows.why: Order book of Rs. 777 crore gives 2-3 years of visibility and subsidiaries won about Rs. 191 crore of new government mandates, at about 20% net margin, though the mix is shifting away from infrastructure advisory.

rows.label: NH Investment Rs. 900 crore into Choice Equity Broking
rows.why: Management said the Rs. 900 crore will be received in Q2 FY27 to fund the MTF book and settlement funding, with growth from it showing from Q3 FY27, though no quantified impact was given.

rows.label: Investment banking mandates ~Rs. 6,600 crore over 1.5 years
rows.why: Roughly Rs. 6,600 crore of current mandates are expected to complete over about 1.5 years, but completion depends on IPO market timing, with one IPO done in Q1 FY27 against a Rs. 6,766 crore pipeline.
